question.prompt: A square and a circle have the same area. What is the ratio of the side length of the square to the radius of the circle?

solutions.explanation:
The equal areas let us connect the two lengths using their area formulas. Let \(s>0\) be the square's side length and \(r>0\) the circle's radius, measured in the same units. Then
\[
s^2=\pi r^2.
\]
Because \(r>0\), we can divide by \(r^2\) to obtain
\[
\left(\frac{s}{r}\right)^2=\pi.
\]
The ratio \(s/r\) is positive, so it is the positive square root of \(\pi\). Thus the requested ratio is \(\boxed{\sqrt{\pi}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Equate the areas
